host_about:
We are a mexican couple who has been together for more than 25 years. We have two teenagers: a daughter, a son.
We are in the IT business and we love to travel. We always travel as if it was the last trip of our lives. For us, family, love and harmony are essential in life. We enjoy contemporary art and we are dedicated to promoting mexican artists and culture in every place we visit. 
Pancho and I met scuba diving in 1994, therefore the sea, nature and outdoor activities are basic and necessary. We enjoy camping, scuba diving and sailing, sport in which we compete every month in Acapulco.
Lunch time is a special moment for us, a pause where we can enjoy and celebrate being together, a moment apart from the rush of the city where we prepare ourselves for the afternoon daily commitments.
We love Mexico and we are ambassadors of our country, we always talk about how great is the mexican spirit, its culture, gastronomy, nature, beaches and its history. If we had to choose another country to live, it would be Italy for the same reasons we love Mexico.
We recognize ourselves as entrepreneurs because of our professional upbringing, we generate projects and ideas, some of which become business ventures. We've always been motivated by the risk, investing time, money and effort to develop new ideas with a purposeful end. Another factor deeply rooted in our family is ecology and self sustainability and seek to have the least possible impact on our environment and our planet .
We have a francophile part because the 4 of Pancho's grandparents were born in France and married in Mexico . With some friends, we spontaneously create an amateur theater group fifteen years ago, "Théâtre a la Dérive", where we enjoy making plays in French just for the pleasure of the whole process, costumes, learning the script and friendship. The group is composed mainly by frenchies living in México.
Today what bring us here is that 14 years ago, on a sabathical year, we lived in a "Chateau" in France countryside, and we opened 11 rooms to host our beloved...  more than a hundred friends and family members came to visit and stayed with us in that 12th century castle. The uniqueness of this experience led us to replicate the model in Mexico, and we open our home with a project: Art Residence to share it with you, people with similar interests, that want to enjoy living among art in our village of San Angel,  town founded 500 years ago and today immersed in one of the largest and most exciting cities in the world: Mexico City. Welcome!

In our country we say to our guests: "Mi casa es tu casa. My home is your home".

_________________________

Roma Norte, as you've probably already read, is full of cafes, galleries, quaint parks, etc. It's safe and beautiful. Our neighborhood was built by the aristocracy of Mexico City in the late 1800s / early 1900s, and the colonial architecture remains. Roma suffered quite a bit of damage following the earthquake of 1985 (as well as in 2018), but in the past decade has seen a rapid revitalization and the opening of many of the city's best restaurants and galleries. We're just a quick walk from Condesa, another beautiful neighborhood with lots to see and do. Colonia Juarez is also up-and-coming, and just 3 blocks away.

neighborhood_overview:
Colonia Roma has the pride of being, together with the Condesa, the first residential development with all the necessary infrastructure services. Three factors that distinguish it from its contemporaries were conjugated in it: the urban, with notable wide streets with camels, tree-lined avenues. Two squares were traced in the north-south central Axis of the colony: Parque Roma (Plaza Rio de Janeiro), and Plaza Ajusco (Luis Cabrera).

The second is its architecture, since in it the last buildings were built in the art nouveau, eclectic and French style that characterized the regime of Porfirio Díaz. Around 1,500 properties are still preserved and converted into artistic monuments.
In the 90s, a series of art galleries, bookstores, museums, and schools are established, starting to continue developing a cultural profile.

host_about:
We are a mexican couple who has been together for more than 25 years. We have two teenagers: a daughter, a son.
We are in the IT business and we love to travel. We always travel as if it was the last trip of our lives. For us, family, love and harmony are essential in life. We enjoy contemporary art and we are dedicated to promoting mexican artists and culture in every place we visit. 
Pancho and I met scuba diving in 1994, therefore the sea, nature and outdoor activities are basic and necessary. We enjoy camping, scuba diving and sailing, sport in which we compete every month in Acapulco.
Lunch time is a special moment for us, a pause where we can enjoy and celebrate being together, a moment apart from the rush of the city where we prepare ourselves for the afternoon daily commitments.
We love Mexico and we are ambassadors of our country, we always talk about how great is the mexican spirit, its culture, gastronomy, nature, beaches and its history. If we had to choose another country to live, it would be Italy for the same reasons we love Mexico.
We recognize ourselves as entrepreneurs because of our professional upbringing, we generate projects and ideas, some of which become business ventures. We've always been motivated by the risk, investing time, money and effort to develop new ideas with a purposeful end. Another factor deeply rooted in our family is ecology and self sustainability and seek to have the least possible impact on our environment and our planet .
We have a francophile part because the 4 of Pancho's grandparents were born in France and married in Mexico . With some friends, we spontaneously create an amateur theater group fifteen years ago, "Théâtre a la Dérive", where we enjoy making plays in French just for the pleasure of the whole process, costumes, learning the script and friendship. The group is composed mainly by frenchies living in México.
Today what bring us here is that 14 years ago, on a sabathical year, we lived in a "Chateau" in France countryside, and we opened 11 rooms to host our beloved...  more than a hundred friends and family members came to visit and stayed with us in that 12th century castle. The uniqueness of this experience led us to replicate the model in Mexico, and we open our home with a project: Art Residence to share it with you, people with similar interests, that want to enjoy living among art in our village of San Angel,  town founded 500 years ago and today immersed in one of the largest and most exciting cities in the world: Mexico City. Welcome!

In our country we say to our guests: "Mi casa es tu casa. My home is your home".

host_about:
Holaa!

Greetings from a Mexican heart, my name is Daniel and I’m thrilled to tell you about who I am and what I like.

I speak Spanish, English & Music (yes, it is also a language) I love music, I want to dedicate my life to learning, playing and listening to it around the world. I myself play guitar, piano and sing. 

I am also in the process of writing a book and I’m currently developing an app too.

I’m Buddhist coming from a Jewish family and I will always be up for a good meal and chat. I like to go out as much as I enjoy my own company. I am organized (some would say too much) and I always take care of those I love and matter to me.

I’m currently on a 5 month trip around the USA on a journey to discover my own music as well as the history behind it, while I grow and explore what it means to grow up (I guess we all have to at some point)

I’m very excited to get to know the world and learn from it.

If you’re a host, you read this, and you’re still thinking about taking me in or not, you have to know something very important before you make your mind... 

...I make killer poached eggs.

I hope this arrives well and I’ll be around if you ever want to talk.

Hasta pronto!

host_about:
Desde hace mucho tiempo, tengo la fortuna de vivir en esta casa de los años 50s,  tiene espacios grandes, luminosos, techos altos, y sobre todo innumerables  historias que la llenan de una energía muy especial.
Actualmente  vivo con  mi  pareja Paco, excelente fotógrafo y mi  hijo Carlos, increíble maestro de futbol para niños.  quienes tendremos el gusto de atenderlos y hacer de su estancia una experiencia cálida y práctica.  Por temporadas también están mis hijas María y Aurora, quienes viven fuera.  
Soy  socióloga y educadora,  he sido maestra de kinder durante 30 años
Me  encanta viajar y he logrado conocer muchos rincones de este maravilloso país siendo testigo del valor de nuestra cultura,  nuestra gente y nuestra riqueza natural. Aunque no soy muy conocedora también me apasiona  toda expresión artística como la fotografía,  la pintura, la danza y el teatro.  
Me encantan los libros así que en casa  tengo  una  biblioteca  que cuenta con libros de viajes, arte, literatura y naturaleza, entre otros, que podrán disfrutar  en sus ratos libres.
Siempre me ha gustado que mi casa sea un espacio abierto a quien lo quiera disfrutar y aprovechar,  primero a mi  familia, pues tengo un montón de sobrinos, que entraban y salían,  posteriormente la compartí durante 4 años con una amiga y 2 de mis sobrinos. y a partir de entonces he estado recibiendo jóvenes huéspedes.
El CUARTO MARINO, debe su nombre a una joven pareja que lo ocupó mientras se formaron como buzos y ahora viven en Puerto Morelos, buceando en los arrecifes de coral y con tiburones.
El CUARTO DE LOS ARTISTAS , debe su nombre a que fue utilizado varios años por un grupo de jóvenes  y talentosos músicos  que crearon su banda de jazz, que actualmente es de  primer nivel.

name: Habitación A estilo Mexicano en San Ángel.
description:
Habitación privada en a separate section of a very nice home located in an alley of the historic San Angel neighborhood.
It is a multicultural space that seeks a healthy lifestyle, conscious learning and committed to creative development in which approximately seven people live permanently, who find in it a place of motivation and inspiration for the development of their projects and initiatives.
neighborhood_overview: San Angel is a neighborhood located south of Mexico City that originated in the 16th century. Since before the arrival of the Spaniards, "Tenanitla” in pre-Hispanic times was already an important town, famous for having supplied large rocks that would be used to carve monuments in the main ceremonial centers of Mexico-Tenochtitlan.
host_about:
Después de años de ejercicio profesional en el ámbito corporativo, me separo con el ánimo de trabajar de manera independiente en actividades relacionadas con la arquitectura, el arte y la ecología. A través de diversos seminarios, talleres y diplomados he ido desarrollando un proyecto que comprende la restauración y comercialización de muebles e inmuebles, ecotecnias, bioconstrucción y cultivo de alimentos para autoconsumo. 

En el transcurso se han sumado grandes amigos que trabajan con temas relacionados con la espiritualidad y la conciencia. 
Lo que fue una idea muy general hoy se ha materializado en un proyecto que se denomina “HECHO ESTA” y tiene su sede en esta pequeña casa en San Ángel.

La casa alberga profesionistas independientes que encuentran en ella un lugar de motivación, inspiración, networking y desarrollo para hacer crecer sus proyectos e iniciativas. Es un espacio multicultural que favorece un estilo de vida saludable y sustentable, la gestación de negocios conscientes y la convivencia fraternal como respuesta positiva a la crisis ambiental y social de la actualidad. 
Deseamos construir una comunidad de aprendizaje, compartiendo prácticas, experiencias e historias de transición, ejercitando la plena consciencia.
Creemos que el cambio cultural se promueve mediante el desarrollo creativo, espiritual e intelectual de aptitudes con un gran sentido de trabajo y esfuerzo en procesos participativos.   

Estamos combinando estancias permanentes con espacios de renta dinámica para potencializar el flujo de energías, personas y vitalidad comunitaria.

host_about:
"A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step" CONFUCIUS 

Mis hijas siempre han amado viajar y conocer diferentes culturas; y yo siempre las he apoyado en que conozcan el mundo. Frente a cada viaje, no puedo evitar preocuparme un poco por tenerlas lejos en países desconocidos para mí. Siempre que las despido deseo con todas mis fuerzas que encuentren personas gentiles que las acompañen en su camino y las ayuden si así lo necesitan. Por ello, siempre que recibo huéspedes en mi casa trato de ser una gran anfitriona, ser esa persona que me gustaría que mis hijas encontraran es sus viajes. 

Amo las plantas y las flores; tomar mi café todas las mañanas en mi terracita viendo mi jardín es una de mis mejores medicinas. Siempre he hecho mucho ejercicio, pero actualmente lo que más hago es nadar y practicar yoga. También disfruto muchísimo cocinar. Mi especialidad: ¡el pozole! 

Tengo pendientes varios viajes por el mundo, así que espero poder ser anfitriona de muchos huéspedes y que muy pronto esos planes de conocer nuevos países se hagan realidad. 

Una de las experiencias que más he disfrutado ha sido viajar a Costa Rica, un jardín gigante para los amantes de la Naturaleza como yo. 

"It's where we go, and what we do when we get there, that tell us who we are". JOYCE CAROL OATES

name: Habitación B estilo Mexicano en San Ángel.
description:
Habitación privada en a separate section of a very nice home located in an alley of the historic San Angel neighborhood.
It is a multicultural space that seeks a healthy lifestyle, conscious learning and committed to creative development in which approximately seven people live permanently, who find in it a place of motivation and inspiration for the development of their projects and initiatives.
neighborhood_overview:
San Angel is a neighborhood located south of Mexico City that originated in the 16th century. Since before the arrival of the Spaniards, "Tenanitla” in pre-Hispanic times was already an important town, famous for having supplied large rocks that would be used to carve monuments in the main ceremonial centers of Mexico-Tenochtitlan.

During the viceroyalty it was home to summer houses of great personalities from New Spain. Its cobblestone alleys, neighborhoods and hamlets, gardens and squares, markets and convents, are imbued with identity and mysticism. It is a magical space of history and tradition considered a site of cultural heritage conservation that has been the inspiration of artists, writers and intellectuals.

Walking you can visit several museums such as Casa Estudio Diego Rivera and Frida Kalho, the Carrillo Gil Modern Art Museum, the Hellenic Cultural Center, the Exconvento del Carmen, the Museum of Mexican Revolutions, Casa del Risco or Casa Isidro Fab
host_about:
Después de años de ejercicio profesional en el ámbito corporativo, me separo con el ánimo de trabajar de manera independiente en actividades relacionadas con la arquitectura, el arte y la ecología. A través de diversos seminarios, talleres y diplomados he ido desarrollando un proyecto que comprende la restauración y comercialización de muebles e inmuebles, ecotecnias, bioconstrucción y cultivo de alimentos para autoconsumo. 

En el transcurso se han sumado grandes amigos que trabajan con temas relacionados con la espiritualidad y la conciencia. 
Lo que fue una idea muy general hoy se ha materializado en un proyecto que se denomina “HECHO ESTA” y tiene su sede en esta pequeña casa en San Ángel.

La casa alberga profesionistas independientes que encuentran en ella un lugar de motivación, inspiración, networking y desarrollo para hacer crecer sus proyectos e iniciativas. Es un espacio multicultural que favorece un estilo de vida saludable y sustentable, la gestación de negocios conscientes y la convivencia fraternal como respuesta positiva a la crisis ambiental y social de la actualidad. 
Deseamos construir una comunidad de aprendizaje, compartiendo prácticas, experiencias e historias de transición, ejercitando la plena consciencia.
Creemos que el cambio cultural se promueve mediante el desarrollo creativo, espiritual e intelectual de aptitudes con un gran sentido de trabajo y esfuerzo en procesos participativos.   

Estamos combinando estancias permanentes con espacios de renta dinámica para potencializar el flujo de energías, personas y vitalidad comunitaria.

neighborhood_overview: Coyoacán is the cultural, artistic, and bohemian epicenter of CDMX and at the same time an easygoing neighborhood full of plazas that feels like a village. Artists like Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera, and Octavio Paz, as well as Trotsky, have made their home here. Less than a 5-10 minute walk we have a forested park (Viveros), several hidden churches and cobblestoned plazas (Santa Catarina), food and arts & crafts markets (Mercado de Coyoacán), world-class cafés (Avellaneda), cantinas (La Coyoacana), and restaurants (Los Danzantes). The subway is also a 10-minute walk away, as is Frida's House museum. We are also a short ride (15 min) from the UNAM University campus (MUAC Art Museum), Carrillo Gil Art Museum, Frida and Diego's Studio Museum, and the upscale San Angel shopping and dining area. Condesa and Roma are a 20-25 min car ride away.

Soy una viajera, como tú… y para mi es muy importante encontrar lugares en los que me sienta bienvenida e inspirada para realizar todas esas actividades únicas que cada ciudad en el mundo tiene para ofrecer. Es por eso que decidí iniciar con la experiencia de ser hospedadora, para poder ser parte de este viaje mágico que solo la Ciudad de México tiene para recibirte. 
 
Los lugares que tengo disponibles para ti, están ubicados en las zonas más bellas y seguras de esta ciudad, donde puedes encontrar desde los mejores restaurantes y antros, hasta los más extraños museos y galerías. Todos esperando a ser descubiertos por ti. Los departamemtos son acogedores, limpios y organizados, gracias a todo el equipo que existe junto a mi. Con quienes podrás contar para cualquier duda que tengas durante tu estancia.
 
Además de mi gusto por ser hospedadora, también soy dentista en Hola Diente y en ambos casos me gusta ayudar a las personas que visitan esta ciudad. Eso me ha llevado a unir ambas vocaciones y encontrar el TURISMO DENTAL. Así que si tienes una emergencia dental o incluso si quieres una limpieza antes de tu próxima aventura, en Hola Diente estaremos encantados de ayudar.

Espero que puedas disfrutar de tu estancia en Ciudad de México, junto con los lugares de  hospedaje que tengo para ti. Bienvenidx.

neighborhood_overview: Today, the area is part of the extensive downtown extension of Mexico City, just southeast of the Historic Center. In the past, this area was at the eastern end of the Aztec city-island Mexico-Tenochtitlán, facing Lake Xochimilco. The area was full of artificial islands called chinampas for agriculture and service ports to the thousands of canoes and boats that passed by on their way to the city's markets, especially the main market of Tlatelolco. The exchange traffic decreased after the Conquest of Mexico, but it continued to be very important. However, during the colonial period, the lake and areas of chinampas dried up slowly. By the 19th century, the area had only canals, with the main Canal de la Viga, limiting river traffic.

host_about:
We are a mexican couple who has been together for more than 25 years. We have two teenagers: a daughter, a son.
We are in the IT business and we love to travel. We always travel as if it was the last trip of our lives. For us, family, love and harmony are essential in life. We enjoy contemporary art and we are dedicated to promoting mexican artists and culture in every place we visit. 
Pancho and I met scuba diving in 1994, therefore the sea, nature and outdoor activities are basic and necessary. We enjoy camping, scuba diving and sailing, sport in which we compete every month in Acapulco.
Lunch time is a special moment for us, a pause where we can enjoy and celebrate being together, a moment apart from the rush of the city where we prepare ourselves for the afternoon daily commitments.
We love Mexico and we are ambassadors of our country, we always talk about how great is the mexican spirit, its culture, gastronomy, nature, beaches and its history. If we had to choose another country to live, it would be Italy for the same reasons we love Mexico.
We recognize ourselves as entrepreneurs because of our professional upbringing, we generate projects and ideas, some of which become business ventures. We've always been motivated by the risk, investing time, money and effort to develop new ideas with a purposeful end. Another factor deeply rooted in our family is ecology and self sustainability and seek to have the least possible impact on our environment and our planet .
We have a francophile part because the 4 of Pancho's grandparents were born in France and married in Mexico . With some friends, we spontaneously create an amateur theater group fifteen years ago, "Théâtre a la Dérive", where we enjoy making plays in French just for the pleasure of the whole process, costumes, learning the script and friendship. The group is composed mainly by frenchies living in México.
Today what bring us here is that 14 years ago, on a sabathical year, we lived in a "Chateau" in France countryside, and we opened 11 rooms to host our beloved...  more than a hundred friends and family members came to visit and stayed with us in that 12th century castle. The uniqueness of this experience led us to replicate the model in Mexico, and we open our home with a project: Art Residence to share it with you, people with similar interests, that want to enjoy living among art in our village of San Angel,  town founded 500 years ago and today immersed in one of the largest and most exciting cities in the world: Mexico City. Welcome!

In our country we say to our guests: "Mi casa es tu casa. My home is your home".

I enjoy getting in a good workout, whether it is through martial arts, yoga, skateboarding, or surfing. Sitting down and talking to different people from different cultures and backgrounds is helping me to grow as a person the most!

I am looking forward to hearing from you soon.

neighborhood_overview:
Colorful Roma is the hipster heart of Mexico City. Just west of Centro Historico and hugging the eastern edge of the Condesa neighborhood, Roma is the perfect place to stay if you’re looking to shop at cute boutiques, sip incredibly good coffee, and enjoy close proximity to many of Mexico City’s biggest attractions.

Originally a neighborhood for Mexico City’s upper-class, Roma fell on hard times after the 1985 earthquake. Happily, the neighborhood has enjoyed a recent renaissance—locals love Roma’s combination of art deco mansions, colorful street art, and, of course, the neighborhood’s hipster vibe. Most of Mexico City is safe, and Roma is considered one of the safest neighborhoods in town.

Young artists and longtime residents enjoy traditional food in places like the classic La Polar where you eat one of the best beers in Mexico (Lively local known because it serves beer in a simple environment and with live mariachi music.) - La Birria is a dish native to Cocula, is very representative and part of the gastronomy of the Mexican state of Jalisco.

WHEN TO VISIT MEXICO CITY

neighborhood_overview:
The village of Santa Cruz Atoyac dates from pre-Hispanic times, so it has very ancient traditions and annual festivals of the village, especially that of May 3. It is a safe neighborhood, as it is located in the Benito Juarez mayor, which is located within the safest in Mexico City. The neighborhood has market, super markets, pharmacies, banks and many local shops to be able to eat and entertain.

The old neighborhood of Santa Cruz Atoyac, recognized as one of the original towns of Mexico City, was a part of the route that Hernán Cortés used to get from the city center to his home in Coyoacán. Also in this old house the renowned actress María Rubio lived, where she practiced every day for her performances. Around Casa Vieja there are tourist places, a 5-minute drive or 20-minute walk away is the Frida Kahlo museum, leaving the Cineteca Nacional. Another nearby site is downtown Coyoacan, one of the most visited squares in the City. A few blocks away is Parque de los Venados.

neighborhood_overview:
Be part of the transformation of a neighborhood that is modernizing but that maintains its authenticity and its history alive. The Granada neighborhood was founded in the thirties of the past century with a marked industrial profile due to its proximity to the Cuernavaca Railroad in the north and the San Joaquín River to the south. At that time, the Cervecería Modelo (don't miss the spectacular mural by Pedro Friedeberg outside the plant, a 5-minute walk from the property), Harinas Elizondo and many other industries were established. The Mercado de la Granada and the María Auxilio de los Cristianos Chapel -two blocks from the building- still maintain the architecture of the thirties as well as the Spanish Hospital. Today the neighborhood combines new constructions and businesses typical of the real estate boom in the area with the tradition and folklore that make it unique.

We recommend you to stroll through the Granada market where you can enjoy the best seafood in the area

name: Room with private patio and bathroom
description:
Nice and sunny room with private patio and bathroom full of plants in beautiful Art Deco flat in San Rafael.

The flat is located in one of the most beautiful neighbourhoods of the city. It is a very authentic Mexican neighbourhood, just a few minutes walking distance from Reforma, Santa Maria and the historic centre. Close to Roma-Condesa too.

I am very happy to welcome you in my flat with my cat and I hope to share with you my love for Mexico.
neighborhood_overview:
If you are looking for an authentically Mexican colonia that is close to both the trendy areas (Roma/Condesa) and the historic centre and very well connected to the rest of the city, colonia San Rafael is for you.

It is a colonia that was built in the 19th century, during the Porfiriato, as well as La Roma. That is why you will find many neoclassical, art nouveau, art deco and modernist style buildings, among others.

The neighbourhood is quiet and safe and around the corner you will find many restaurants, bakeries and shops.

There is a metro station two blocks away, Ecobici stations at the corner of the street (the city's bike-sharing system) and also a metrobus station.

Transfer times to points of interest in the city:
- Monumento a la Revolución : 3min by bike / 10min walk
- Colonia Juarez : 7min by bike / 20min walk
- Angel de la Independencia : 10min cycling / 25min walking
- Bellas Artes : 10min by metro or bike / 25m

Be part of the transformation of a neighborhood that is modernizing but that maintains its authenticity and its history alive. The Granada neighborhood was founded in the thirties of the past century with a marked industrial profile due to its proximity to the Cuernavaca Railroad in the north and the San Joaquín River to the south. At that time, the Cervecería Modelo (don't miss the spectacular mural by Pedro Friedeberg outside the plant, a 5-minute walk from the property), Harinas Elizondo and many other industries were established. The Mercado de la Granada and the María Auxilio de los Cristianos Chapel -two blocks from the building- still maintain the architecture of the thirties as well as the Spanish Hospital. Today the neighborhood combines new constructions and businesses typical of the real estate boom in the area with the tradition and folklore that make it unique.

We recommend you to stroll through the Granada market where you can enjoy the best seafood in the area

name: Zebra Suite in Casa Pani
description: From this central home, the whole group will have easy access to everything.
neighborhood_overview: Información acerca del vecindario no proporcionada
host_about:
Casa Pani is an elegant Guest House situated in the beautiful and peaceful, residential yet central area of Cuauhtémoc. 
Casa Pani is close to museums, restaurants, parks and yet only twenty minutes from the airport. 
Casa Pani sits on a quiet street close to a magnificent mid-century church with a charming park at the end of the street.
Originally a private house designed by celebrated Mexican architect Mario Pani and finished in 1962. The house has been restored and updated, respecting the original materials and identity of Pani. 
In addition to the 1962 house, a 2019 New House has been thoughtfully designed to reflect and honor Mario Pani’s original house. The New House is set on the other side of the existing two outdoor patios and is connected through a covered walkway.
The two houses together offer six private bedrooms each with bathrooms on suite and all with direct access to light and air. 
There are three large connecting reception rooms. 
Two rooftop terraces. Each bedroom has a Dyson air purifier heater and air cooler. On the ground floor there is an indoor-outdoor dipping pool, a bar and a fully equipped stainless steel chef’s kitchen.
Our furnishings have been thoughtfully selected and include classic pieces by both Mexican and international artists and designers.

neighborhood_overview:
Colorful Roma is the hipster heart of Mexico City. Just west of Centro Historico and hugging the eastern edge of the Condesa neighborhood, Roma is the perfect place to stay in if you’re looking to shop at cute boutiques, sip incredibly good coffee, and enjoy close proximity to many of Mexico City’s biggest attractions.

Originally a neighborhood for Mexico City’s upper-class, Roma fell on hard times after the 1985 earthquake. Happily, the neighborhood has enjoyed a recent renaissance—locals love Roma’s combination of art deco mansions, colorful street art, and, of course, the neighborhood’s hipster vibe. Most of Mexico City is safe, and Roma is considered one of the safest neighborhoods in town.
